pass_a_gloss: …thymiaama / incense… asēptōn xylōn / unrotting woods… kerata / horns = stauros / cross… hōraios kallei / fair in beauty… mathētai / disciples carriers…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …of the veil that is upon the ark of the testimony, in which I will be known to you there as God; and Aaron will burn upon it compound thin incense in the morning, morning; when he overshadows the lamps, he will burn upon it. And when Aaron lights the lamps at evening, he will burn upon it incense of continuity through all before the Lord unto their generations. And you will not bring up upon it another incense; a fruit of sacrifice, and a drink-offering you will not pour upon it. And Aaron will propitiate upon it upon its horns, once of the year from the blood of the cleansing of the sins of the propitiation. Once of the year he will cleanse it unto their generations; it is Holy of holies to the Lord.’
Palladius: Will we then also receive this unto a type of Christ?

Cyril: Very much so, O Palladius. For it is true that the matter is his honored and deep mystery; it would show also very easily to those who have chosen to busy themselves with such things thinly and with a file. For it had been made from unrotting woods, and had been entirely anointed with gold. For the body of Christ is incorruptible, and enriched in itself with the divine nature; ‘For the Word became flesh, and tented among us.’ And Christ is our firstfruit, and a root of the race being remade unto incorruption through the union toward God, even if the matter should be understood exceptionally upon him. And horns for the altar, and as hands stretched out, and pre-molding the shape of the honored cross. And if someone should say the horns are four, it wrongs nothing, at least unto understanding uprightly for the one loving to learn. For the altar happening to be square and equal-sided everywhere, the sight of the horns is equal from every side; and what is the word of this? For in every place Christ is known, and this one crucified; and this is a bright boast for those who believe unto him. And indeed the divine Paul, ‘And for me may it not become to boast, except in the cross of Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.’ And there has been added to the craft the things finishing unto adornment—a twisted crown; for truly ‘Fair in beauty beside the sons of humans’ is Emmanuel. And the things unto need for it have also been brought on—the carriers and the rest. For the divine altar needed to be carried in the world according to the times of the breakings-camp. And the divine disciples were also doing this, carrying Christ around through the preaching both seemly and according to order, as servants of God and stewards of mysteries of Christ. ‘And you will set,’ he says, ‘the altar opposite the veil that is upon the ark of the testimonies, in which I will be known to you from there.’
Palladius: Then what is the necessary also of the places themselves, I think, that have been ordered?
Cyril: How deep the word, and very dim; yet I will say as is possible, trusting God who also makes wise
